article_title: Hybrid Deep Learning Model to Estimate Cognitive Effort from fNIRS Signals
citation: Shayla Sharmin and Roghayeh Leila Barmaki. 2025. Hybrid Deep Learning Model to Estimate Cognitive Effort from fNIRS Signals. Companion Proceedings of the 27th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction (ICMI Companion '25). https://doi.org/10.1145/3747327.3764901
title: Cognitive effort measured through Relative Neural Efficiency (RNE) and Relative Neural Involvement (RNI) combining brain activity and performance
description: The article applies a cognitive effort framework in which brain activity alone cannot distinguish focus from struggle, so effort is assessed by combining neural activity with performance. Two z-scored metrics are derived: RNE, where "High RNE means good performance with less effort", and RNI, which "shows how engaged or motivated a person is". The study computes these from fNIRS-derived oxygenated hemoglobin and quiz scores in an educational game to detect efficient learning, engagement, and cognitive fatigue.
requirements: Requires both a performance score and a hemodynamic response measure, converted to z-scores to bring effort and performance onto the same scale
constraints: An epsilon constant (0.001) is added to the z-score denominator to avoid division by zero when performance standard deviation is zero
target_learners: adult participants in an educational quiz game study
target_learning_goals: monitoring cognitive effort, efficiency, and engagement during learning tasks
examples: RNE and RNI were computed from z-scored quiz performance and mean PFC oxygenated hemoglobin for each participant and segment
